summary.intent: Recover lost Phase 37 (parallel batch upload pipeline) roadmap entry, capture implementation decisions via discuss-phase workflow, then research and plan the phase.
summary.outcome: Phase 37 context was captured with all key decisions locked in CONTEXT.md, research completed and RESEARCH.md written, but the planning step (PLAN.md generation) was cut short by a usage limit mid-agent execution.

repo: Phase 37 was added to ROADMAP.md and its directory created during a prior session but was never committed — it existed only as unstaged local changes when the session started.

The current upload pipeline in useDropUpload.ts loops sequentially: each file calls client.uploadFile() which does encrypt → IPFS pin → add FilePointer → publish folder IPNS, resulting in N IPNS publishes for N files.

The SDK's withOperation() serializes all SDK operations, meaning concurrent calls to uploadFile() would just queue — making Option C (web-layer batching via existing API) non-viable for true parallelism.

The desktop FUSE layer receives files one-at-a-time via filesystem release() callbacks and has no batch context, so it cannot benefit from a batch uploadFiles() method without a separate write-coalescing layer.
The Rust SDK queue.rs handles uploads for desktop via a sequential queue model that is architecturally separate from the web SDK pipeline.

code.finding: Sequential file upload loop — each file calls client.uploadFile() individually, producing N IPNS publishes for N files.
uploadFile() does encrypt+pin+publish as one atomic unit, preventing external batching of the folder update.
FUSE release() callback triggers per-file upload — no batch context available at this layer.
Rust SDK uses a sequential upload queue; desktop upload model is fundamentally one-file-at-a-time.

workflow: The discuss-phase assumptions mode routes through a gsd-assumptions-analyzer subagent to keep raw file contents out of the main context window.
The GSD workflow creates a feature branch before writing any phase artifacts.
ROADMAP.md and STATE.md modifications from planning sessions should be committed promptly — leaving them unstaged risks losing work across sessions.
The plan-phase workflow checks for UI indicators and a UI-SPEC before spawning the planner, acting as a safety gate for frontend phases.

friction: Phase 37 roadmap entry and directory were lost between sessions because they were never committed — required investigation at session start to determine what happened.
The planner agent was cut off mid-execution by a usage limit, leaving PLAN.md unwritten and requiring a respawn.
The discuss-phase flow asked a redundant question about publish timing that had already been answered earlier in the same conversation, causing confusion.
